Use case: stylized-concept.
Project: RAPTOR / Pixel Wing, an aerial arcade game. This is finished presentation artwork for a proposed four-city pixel-art edition.
Style: richly authored 16-bit pixel art with precise stepped diagonals, crisp square pixels, restrained ordered dithering, deliberate color clusters, richly observed miniature details, and clear readable silhouettes. No smooth vector shapes, no photorealism, no painterly brushwork, no voxel 3D, no lens blur, no bloom, no CRT overlay.
Existing game palette: deep ink #10182e, navy #1c2945, slate #465d7a, titanium #dbe5df, mint #95e6db, teal #328e92, warm gold #ffbd6c, coral #ff686b, violet #716692, cream #fff2ce. Environment colors can extend this palette while aircraft and interactive effects remain consistent.
Camera: near-top-down oblique aerial arcade view with visible short building facades and coherent upper-left light. Preserve a useful view of streets, roofs and water rather than a ground-level skyline. One consistent pixel grid. The game uses a 640 by 400 logical canvas.
Presentation quality: dense authored city character, graceful large-scale composition, areas of quieter texture for flight readability. All requested objects fully inside frame. No watermark. No extra logos or invented text.
Primary request: A complete New York City aerial gameplay keyframe. Manhattan is a tapered, densely gridded island framed by the Hudson on its west and East River on its east, with the harbor foreground and Brooklyn opposite the East River. Compress distances artistically while retaining this recognizable water geometry. Show a distinct copper-green Statue of Liberty on detached Liberty Island in the harbor; One World Trade Center's faceted spire in Lower Manhattan; Brooklyn Bridge's Gothic towers and fine suspension cables crossing the East River; Empire State Building's stepped crown farther uptown; and a green Central Park rectangle in the upper distance. City blocks have rooftop water tanks, brick setbacks, gold window clusters, tiny yellow taxis, waterfront piers and a few orange ferries with pixel wakes. Blue-hour navy water, steel-blue buildings, plum shadows, warm window accents. Avoid duplicating landmarks. One small titanium F-22, nose pointing toward the top, over the harbor near the lower-middle of frame; tiny coral enemy drones far ahead and two narrow gold projectile trails establish scale without hiding landmarks. No historical disaster scene. No HUD or text. Fill the image edge to edge; this is one coherent scene, not a collage.

Primary request: A complete San Francisco aerial gameplay keyframe. Compose a hilly peninsula, with bay water to the east, the Golden Gate strait to the northwest, and ocean beyond the western shoreline. Use deliberate arcade spatial compression. The unmistakable vermilion Golden Gate suspension bridge spans the strait to green Marin hills; do not put it across the eastern bay. Put the slender white Transamerica Pyramid in the downtown cluster, Coit Tower on a separate rounded Telegraph Hill, and the Ferry Building's clocktower on the eastern waterfront. An offshore Alcatraz island sits inside the bay. Repeated pastel Victorian houses climb terraced streets, diagonal Market Street cuts the grid, tiny burgundy-and-cream cable cars cross a hill, piers stripe the waterfront, and one small crooked street winds through a block. Morning light, eucalyptus greens, cream roofs, cool teal water, lavender building shadows. Discrete low fog bands over the strait with hard pixel-cluster edges leave bridge towers and all aircraft readable. One small titanium F-22, nose pointing toward the top, crosses water near the lower-middle of frame; tiny coral hostile drones farther up and two narrow gold projectile trails. No HUD or text. Fill the image edge to edge as one coherent scene.

Primary request: A complete Austin, Texas aerial gameplay keyframe. The broad blue-green curve of Lady Bird Lake crosses the foreground, with downtown north of the lake and low colorful South Congress blocks south of it. Congress Avenue Bridge crosses the lake; Congress Avenue continues as a visible street spine toward the rose-granite Texas State Capitol and its dome inland. Compress distances artistically while keeping lake, bridge, downtown and Capitol relationships legible. Include a faceted contemporary downtown tower cluster without turning the city into Manhattan; warm limestone roofs, little music-club fronts, colorful food-trailer courtyards, sidewalks, live-oak canopies, waterside trails, and a few kayaks with tiny wakes. A fine ribbon of tiny black bats emerges from underneath Congress Avenue Bridge against open dusk sky reflections on the lake, never confused with projectiles. Peach-and-violet sunset light, rose-granite Capitol, teal lake, long dark-violet shadows and restrained amber city lights. One small titanium F-22, nose pointing toward the top, above open water near the lower-middle of frame; a few tiny coral hostile drones farther ahead and two narrow gold projectile trails. No desert canyon, cactus landscape, or western saloon stereotype. No HUD or text. Fill the image edge to edge as one coherent scene.

Primary request: A complete Washington, DC aerial gameplay keyframe. The National Mall is a broad green east-west axis: Lincoln Memorial at the west end, its long rectangular Reflecting Pool immediately east, the tall narrow Washington Monument obelisk farther east, and the domed U.S. Capitol at the far eastern end. Keep all four silhouettes clearly separate and geographically ordered. Show the curving Tidal Basin south of the axis, its Jefferson Memorial rotunda at the southern shore, and the broader Potomac toward the west. Use deliberate arcade spatial compression. Include rows of pale-pink cherry blossoms around the basin, low rectangular museum roofs, the red Smithsonian Castle, broad stone terraces, diagonal avenues and traffic circles, precise lawn paths and tiny paddleboats. A low-rise ivory city, spring-green lawns, desaturated aqua water, cobalt shadows, crisp morning daylight. No Manhattan skyscrapers, no duplicate domes, no bridge through the reflecting pool. One small titanium F-22, nose pointing toward the top, over open water near the lower-middle of frame; a few small coral hostile drones farther ahead and two narrow gold projectile trails, leaving the architecture readable. Primary request: Create finished title-screen key art for RAPTOR's pixel-art edition. One beautifully drawn titanium F-22 with angular wings, twin tails, a dark mint-reflecting canopy and two modest orange exhausts banks across the center foreground. Behind it is an intentional four-panel city panorama: New York harbor with Liberty and a stepped skyscraper, San Francisco's orange Golden Gate Bridge and hills, Austin's lake and rose Capitol dome, Washington's obelisk and white Capitol. Each panel is a distinct city, separated by narrow ink-colored rules, not a single geographically impossible city. Large shapes read at thumbnail size while close inspection rewards miniature city details. Keep the upper quarter relatively quiet dark navy for a title that will be typeset separately. Match the near-top-down aerial city language but allow a more dramatic three-quarter aircraft pose for the title art. No text, no letters, no UI buttons.

Primary request: A finished pixel-art aircraft design sheet on flat deep-ink background, aligned in a spacious regular grid with no text. Main subject is an unmistakable compact F-22: faceted titanium body, trapezoid wings, two canted tails, dark canopy with mint highlight, two small orange exhausts; nose points upward. First row: the same fighter at neutral, shallow left bank, deep left bank, shallow right bank and deep right bank, all equal scale. Second row: six clear progressive dodge-roll poses of that same fighter. Third row: normal exhaust, afterburner exhaust, light damage smoke, severe damage smoke, mint recovery/invulnerability outline, and separate low-contrast ground shadow. Bottom row: one larger three-quarter inspection view with no ground, a matching allied fighter with mint ID marks, a neutral twin-engine transport with cream livery, and a small reconnaissance drone. Every silhouette separated by generous empty gutters; use only subtle panel rules, no checkerboard transparency. Consistent light direction, true small-scale game-sprite shapes, restrained detail. A visual design reference sheet, not a claimed engine-ready animation atlas.

Primary request: A finished pixel-art enemy and boss art sheet on deep-ink navy background, spacious two-tier composition with subtle panel rules and no text. Upper tier has four small readable enemy silhouettes: swept-wing interceptor, dart drone, heavier twin-engine bomber, armored coastal gunboat; each predominantly slate and dark violet with coral identification marks, upward player and downward enemies distinguished by nose direction. Include neutral and flash/damaged versions beside each. Lower tier contains four large fictional arcade boss designs, all distinct and seen in the same near-top-down perspective: a broad flying command carrier for New York; a long twin-hull arsenal vessel for San Francisco's bay; a wide winged drone-launcher aircraft for Austin; and an angular stealth command wing flanked by small drones for Washington DC. Show modular coral-highlighted weapon hardpoints, ivory specular edges, intact state and a smaller damaged state with pixel smoke beside each. Avoid using civic landmarks as enemies. No real military insignia, text, people, giant robots, or extraterrestrial ships. Bosses must be readable machines assembled from deliberate pixel clusters, with generous space between silhouettes.

New York quadrant: detached Liberty Island with statue, Brooklyn Bridge module with two Gothic towers, stepped Empire State crown, faceted One World Trade Center, dense brick city block, rooftop water tanks, yellow taxi, ferry and quay. Primary request: Use case: ui-mockup. A polished pixel-art game interface presentation with six equal 8:5 screens in a clean two-column by three-row board on deep ink. Each screen is a coherent designed state for the same aerial game. Screen 1: title artwork with an F-22 over four miniature city bands, exact title 'RAPTOR', subtitle 'PIXEL WING', and one clear 'TAKE FLIGHT' button. Screen 2: region selection with four equal illustrated destination cards captioned exactly 'NEW YORK', 'SAN FRANCISCO', 'AUSTIN', 'WASHINGTON DC', and a selected-card gold frame. Screen 3: mission briefing with a large city mini-map, a clear route line, three compact objective rows and one 'LAUNCH' button; keep secondary copy as short unlabeled graphic rows, no fake paragraphs. Screen 4: live flight over Manhattan with tiny pixel fighter and projectiles, restrained top HUD reading 'SCORE 024800', six mint armor segments, and bottom missile/dodge indicators; most of screen is city artwork. Screen 5: paused flight with a compact centered dark panel, exact 'PAUSED', 'RESUME', 'CONTROLS', 'SETTINGS', small control glyphs. Screen 6: completed flight with exact 'SORTIE COMPLETE', a gold medal, three short stat rows, four city completion chips and 'CONTINUE'. Use legible bitmap typography, mint focus states, gold primary action, coral danger; hard rectangular pixel borders, restrained ornaments. Every screen has consistent typography and spacing. No web browser chrome, no rounded SaaS cards, no body prose, no fake extensive microtext. This is a static visual concept of a proposed game flow, not a functional screenshot.
